ww2:0: September the 1st, 1939. Before dawn, German tanks roll across the Polish border, and dive-bombers fill the sky above them. Watch the red spread out from Germany, the colour of the Axis on this map. Poland's army is brave, but its horses and old guns are no match for this new kind of war, fast and mechanised. And far away in Asia, Japan has already been at war with China for two years. The Second World War has begun.
ww2:1: Two days later, Britain and France keep their promise to Poland, and declare war on Germany. See how the blue reaches across the world. Their empires come with them, from Canada to India, from Australia to much of Africa. Then, on the 17th of September, the Soviet Union invades Poland from the east, under a secret pact with Hitler. Caught between two great armies, Poland is divided, and disappears from the map once more.
ww2:2: Spring, 1940. After a long, uneasy winter of waiting, Germany strikes north. In a single day, Denmark is taken, and German troops land along the coast of Norway, from Oslo far up to Narvik. The prize is the sea route that carries Swedish iron ore to German factories. Notice how the orange of occupation creeps up the coast of Scandinavia.
ww2:3: May. Germany turns west, and the war that had been waiting comes all at once. German armour slips through the dense forests of the Ardennes, where few expected tanks could pass, and races to the English Channel in just ten days. Follow the arrows to the coast. Trapped on the beaches at Dunkirk, over 338,000 Allied soldiers are carried home across the water, many of them in small fishing boats and pleasure craft.
ww2:4: June. Hitler's troops march into Paris, and the city falls without a fight. France is now divided, with the north under German occupation, shown here in orange. In Rome, Mussolini declares war, and brings Italy's lands in Africa into the fight. For now, most of France's colonies follow the new government at Vichy. And across the Channel, Britain stands almost alone.
battle:plassey: Bengal, June 1757. Near the village of Palashi, about 3,000 soldiers of the East India Company, under Robert Clive, face an army of some 50,000 led by the nawab, Siraj ud-Daulah. But Clive has made a secret deal. He has promised Bengal's throne to the nawab's own commander, Mir Jafar, and when the moment comes, Mir Jafar's troops simply stand and watch. A monsoon downpour soaks the nawab's gunpowder, while the Company keeps its own dry. A trading company now holds India's richest province, and almost two centuries of British power in India have begun.
voyage:magellan-elcano:intro: In September 1519, five ships slip out of the mouth of the Guadalquivir, in southern Spain. Their captain, Ferdinand Magellan, is Portuguese, sailing for the Spanish crown, and he means to reach the Spice Islands by sailing west. About 270 men are aboard. Three years from now, one ship, and just 18 of them, will come home.
voyage:magellan-elcano:0: Sanlúcar de Barrameda. The five ships leave the river mouth behind, and the coast of Spain falls away over the stern.
voyage:magellan-elcano:1: December, on the coast of Brazil. In the bay of Rio de Janeiro, the fleet takes two weeks of rest and trade, before the long run south.
voyage:magellan-elcano:2: Far to the south, in Patagonia, winter closes in. For months the fleet waits at Puerto San Julián. A mutiny is crushed there, and one ship is wrecked on the coast.
voyage:magellan-elcano:3: October 1520. At last, a passage opens through the tip of South America. For 38 days the ships thread their way through cold, twisting channels, and one of them turns back for home. The strait still carries Magellan's name.
